# dsm_scheduled_task (Data Source)

Reads an existing task from DSM Task Scheduler.

Reading a task executes nothing, so this data source is not gated behind `allow_task_execution`. It is a useful way to see what a NAS is already configured to run — including tasks created by hand in DSM — before deciding whether to manage them from Terraform.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Reading a task executes nothing, so this works without allow_task_execution.
data "dsm_scheduled_task" "prune_images" {
  name = "docker-prune"
}

output "prune_command" {
  description = "What the NAS is currently configured to run, and as whom."
  value       = "${data.dsm_scheduled_task.prune_images.user}: ${data.dsm_scheduled_task.prune_images.command}"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Task name to look up. DSM does not require task names to be unique; an ambiguous name is an error rather than an arbitrary match.

### Read-Only

- `command` (String) Shell command DSM executes.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the task is active.
- `id` (String) Numeric task identifier assigned by DSM, as a string.
- `notify_email` (String) Address DSM emails when the task runs, or null when notification is disabled.
- `notify_on_failure` (Boolean) Whether DSM notifies only on failure rather than after every run.
- `real_owner` (String) Account DSM records as the owner of the task entry.
- `schedule` (Attributes) When the task runs. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--schedule))
- `type` (String) DSM task type, such as `script` or `service`. Only `script` tasks can be managed by the `dsm_scheduled_task` resource; the others are DSM's own built-in maintenance tasks.
- `user` (String) Account DSM runs the command as.

<a id="nestedatt--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `schedule`

Read-Only:

- `day_of_week` (Set of String) Weekday names the task runs on.
- `frequency` (String) `daily`, `weekly`, or `monthly`.
- `hour` (Number) Hour the task starts.
- `minute` (Number) Minute the task starts.
- `repeat_interval_hours` (Number) Same-day repeat interval in hours, or 0 when disabled.
- `repeat_interval_minutes` (Number) Same-day repeat interval in minutes, or 0 when disabled.
- `repeat_until_hour` (Number) Last hour of the day at which a same-day repeat may still fire.
- `week_of_month` (Set of String) Weeks of the month a monthly task runs in.
